scope: Bounded source and visual audit of two stroke-only metal-tool inscriptions; no semantic or phonetic reading.
blindness: Not blinded: prior Pettersson 4i4t and 7i4t claims were known. OCR used to find original pages; claims checked on page images.

initial_locator_correction.result: Not the targets: p489 identifies item1 as spear-head DK7858 and item4 as axe DK7853. No inscription patches visible on those drawings. Correct target locators are CXXVII1 and CXXXIII1. This does not assert those non-target objects were uninscribed on every physical surface.

rows.photographs: FEM CXXXI38 and39, explicitly joined by p460
rows.type: Spear-head (?) in table; p460 also suggests a large double-edged knife. Functional uncertainty retained.
rows.dimension_caveat: Restored/unfolded length; estimated width. Table tang thickness 0.11 versus prose greatest thickness near tang 0.13 retained without harmonization.

drawn_mark_groups.position: above and slightly right of seven-mark group
drawn_mark_groups.orientation: upright strokes in a tilted light rectangular patch; not a four-horizontal-stroke stack in this drawing
upright strokes in near-horizontal light strip

rows.nonstroke_signs: None depicted on the CXXVII1 drawing. Three round perforations are object features, not promoted to signs.
rows.primary_text_counts: Two rows, one of four and other of seven; p460 does not specify vertical/horizontal contrast.
rows.photo_reading: Folded blade and perforations visible. Corrosion/contrast prevent an independent recount and orientation assignment to all eleven strokes.
rows.mass_evidence: p454 explicitly calls weighing CXXVII1 useless owing to its thinness and oxidation; no numeric mass supplied there.
rows.comparison_with_later_notation: Pettersson defines4t as a tilted row, not necessarily four individually horizontal strokes. The tilted upper group is compatible with that notation; the earlier assertion of a source conflict on this basis is withdrawn. Numerical meaning and equality of this group with knife/tang groups remain unproved.

rows.type: Knife, very badly corroded; no fresh functional classification.

locus.house_reading: Ditto from preceding catalogue row, not a separate printed VI on target row.

rows.primary_text_counts: p463 explicitly describes eight strokes in a close group: four vertical just above four horizontal.
rows.photo_reading: Photo shows corroded knife, tang/perforation and marks on upper blade; neither four-plus-four count nor each orientation is independently secure at retained resolution.
rows.nonstroke_signs: No additional complex sign independently identified in photograph. Surface damage prevents proof of absence.
rows.mass_evidence: No numerical mass in reviewed p454,463,493 passages. This is a bounded absence, not an exhaustive museum/conservation search.
rows.comparison_with_later_notation: 4i4t agrees with original prose, but repeated publications are not independent object observations.

limits: Strokes counted on drawing/prose are not identified numeral values.
Published drawing, text and photograph are representations of the same objects, not independent semantic anchors.
The two target objects have different excavation loci and levels; no common hoard inferred for knife.
No physical autopsy or modern independent surface imaging.
No M77 sign crosswalk made in this file; parent audit verifies it independently.

corrections.superseded_text: Pettersson table 7i4t cannot be treated as independently confirmed four transverse strokes from this original drawing. Possible difference in source representation remains unresolved.
corrections.reason: Re-read Pettersson1999 pp98,101: t labels tilted rows. Group layout was incorrectly conflated with individual stroke orientation in our attribution. Original drawing observations unchanged.
